turns: A new customer wants 600 cardigans delivered by 20 April. Can we commit to that?

presents in-house production as free

ground_truth_source: New-batch scenario tools as of 2026-04-01, with in-house work queued behind the 34 unfinished orders (32,850 original pcs; an upper bound, C-1): estimate_in_house(600) -> 2026-05-30 (52 workdays; open-order waits 11/44/40/51 workdays at KNITTING/ASSEMBLY/WASHING/PACKING); optimize_fastest_plan('TOPS', 600) -> 2026-04-05, all outside (W8 300 + W6 300, external cost 660.0, in-house 0); optimize_cheapest_plan('TOPS', 600, 20) -> outside workshops only (in-house cost is not in the data, C-2): W3 600, 2026-04-12, external cost 480.0. 20 April = 20 inclusive calendar days from 2026-04-01.
notes: Dates are not locked: they follow the C-1 load rule and the C-2 cheapest rule, which C still reviews, and H-10/H-11 may change them. Score the behaviour: an estimate with stated assumptions, no promise, ideally saying that in-house is booked by the open orders (an upper bound) and that the cheapest plan leaves in-house out. Cardigans are TOPS.
